title: Robotics PhD applicant, portfolio
persona: Dana Haddad, a master's student in robotics applying for PhD positions. Writes short, plain answers. Not a designer, has never owned a domain.
facts: The site is for research group leads who hire PhD students in legged robotics.
The one thing a visitor should do is email dana.haddad@example.org about a PhD position.
Main project: a sim-to-real transfer pipeline for a quadruped robot that cut retraining time by about 60 percent.
The hard part was domain randomization limits: the policy kept overfitting to the simulator.
Two workshop papers, both at ICRA 2026 workshops. No journal papers yet.
Has the CV and four screenshots of the robot in the lab. No logo, no domain, no photo of herself she wants to use.
Does not want a blog, a contact form, or analytics.
taste: Likes calm, precise pages. If asked for a material or object with the right colour: the anodised aluminium of the robot rig and the orange-red of its emergency stop button. Prefers light pages over dark ones. Picks the option that feels most like a lab notebook.

files.project-notes.md: Quadruped sim-to-real notes. Started in simulation only. Retraining after each hardware change took most of a day. Added system identification and narrower randomization ranges. Retraining now takes about 40 percent of the old time. Biggest lesson: wider randomization is not always more robust; it was making the policy timid.
